title: 45. Numeracy & Number Systems: Calculating a Percentage of a Quantity
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Calculating a Simple Percentage of a Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a simple percentage of a whole-number quantity using the percentage-as-a-fraction method.
questions.question: What is \(25\%\) of \(80\)?
questions.hint: Rewrite \(25\%\) as a simple fraction, then multiply by the quantity.

questions.concept: Calculating a Percentage of a Quantity Using a Decimal
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a percentage of a quantity by converting the percentage to a decimal.
questions.question: What is \(15\%\) of \(200\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(15\%\) to \(0.15\). Then calculate \(0.15\times200=30\). Therefore, \(15\%\) of \(200\) is \(30\).
questions.hint: Convert the percentage to a decimal by dividing by \(100\), then multiply by the quantity.

questions.concept: Calculating a Percentage of a Quantity by Decomposition
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a percentage of a quantity by decomposing the percentage into convenient parts.
questions.question: What is \(40\%\) of \(75\)?
questions.hint: Find \(10\%\) of the quantity first, then scale that result to \(40\%\).

questions.concept: Calculating a Fractional Percentage of a Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Use an equivalent fraction to calculate a percentage of a quantity efficiently.
questions.question: What is \(12.5\%\) of \(64\)?
questions.hint: Express \(12.5\%\) as a familiar unit fraction before multiplying.

questions.concept: Calculating a Percentage of a Larger Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a two-digit percentage of a three-digit whole-number quantity accurately.
questions.question: What is \(35\%\) of \(240\)?
questions.hint: Convert \(35\%\) to a decimal and multiply it by \(240\).

questions.concept: Calculating a Decimal Percentage of a Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a percentage containing a decimal part of a whole-number quantity.
questions.question: What is \(7.5\%\) of \(320\)?
questions.hint: Divide the percentage by \(100\) before multiplying by the quantity.

questions.concept: Calculating a Percentage Greater Than 100 of a Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a percentage greater than 100 of a given quantity and interpret the result.
questions.question: What is \(120\%\) of \(45\)?
questions.explanation: \(120\%=1.2\). Therefore, \(120\%\) of \(45\) is \(1.2\times45=54\). Because \(120\%\) is greater than \(100\%\), the result is greater than \(45\).
questions.hint: Convert \(120\%\) to a decimal by dividing by \(100\), then multiply by the quantity.

questions.concept: Calculating a Small Percentage of a Quantity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a small decimal percentage of a whole-number quantity accurately.
questions.question: What is \(2.5\%\) of \(360\)?
questions.hint: Convert \(2.5\%\) to a decimal carefully before multiplying by \(360\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate percentages of two different quantities and compare the resulting amounts.
questions.question: Class A collected \(240\) recyclable items, and \(35\%\) were plastic. Class B collected \(180\) recyclable items, and \(40\%\) were plastic. How many more plastic items did Class A collect than Class B?
questions.explanation: For Class A, \(35\%\) of \(240\) is \(0.35\times240=84\). For Class B, \(40\%\) of \(180\) is \(0.40\times180=72\). The difference is \(84-72=12\). Therefore, Class A collected \(12\) more plastic items.
questions.hint: Calculate the percentage amount for each class separately, then compare the two results.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate successive percentages of quantities in a multi-step situation.
questions.question: A factory produces \(800\) components. During inspection, \(15\%\) are set aside for additional testing. Of those components, \(20\%\) are selected for a detailed test. How many components are selected for the detailed test?
questions.explanation: First calculate \(15\%\) of \(800\): \(0.15\times800=120\). Then calculate \(20\%\) of \(120\): \(0.20\times120=24\). Therefore, \(24\) components are selected for the detailed test.
questions.hint: First find the number set aside for additional testing. Then take the second percentage of that smaller quantity.
